root_cause: No existing authoritative preflight invocation history covers a generated ID whose producer invocation fails before writing its target artifact. Target nonexistence proves only path availability.

read_only_forensics.authorization_lifecycle_ledger: evaluation/v1_2_3/authorization_lifecycle_events.jsonl; tracks authorization lifecycle, not preflight IDs
read_only_forensics.transaction_journals: evaluation/v4_runs/.execution_transactions; track authorization, attempt, namespace and transaction identities, not preflight IDs
read_only_forensics.attempt_ledgers_and_namespace_markers: evaluation/v4_runs; track formal attempts and namespace claims, not preflight IDs
read_only_forensics.preflight_artifacts: Only cover invocations that produced a target file; cannot cover a failure before artifact write
read_only_forensics.evaluation_audits_and_record: May mention selected invocation IDs, but are not a complete durable claim record for every producer invocation
read_only_forensics.prior_collision_proof_scope: Existing target path collision only; no historical ID claim proof

claim_order: Open existing registry without following symlinks and take an exclusive file lock
Generate candidate UUID4 ID while locked
Strictly parse the append-only registry and reject malformed or duplicate records
Reject historical ID collision even when target is absent
Append claim event, flush and fsync before returning ID and target
Continue read-only eligibility, runtime connectivity and artifact write only after durable claim
repair.crash_semantics: A claim becomes part of the producer invocation lifecycle only after the claim event is fsynced. Crash after that point preserves non-reusability even without a preflight artifact. A torn partial row invalidates the registry and fails closed; a crash before claim durability returns no invocation ID.
